# rework_claims_r5 — cpi_insurance_verification_and_force_placement (audit revision_3; coordinator route round 5)

- R3-A (cm_close_adj tier 2 adds nothing): the closing-day adjustment is removed from both refund rules. No closing-coverage-end factor replaces it. The contract charter counts payoff clearance in business days (Monday to Friday, excluding federal holidays) per payment channel, and the compute cannot reproduce that exactly. The recorded funds_final_date on its own gives a single tier, not a ladder (plan.md "Round 5 design").
- R3-B1 (close-adjustment schedule contradicts payoff_funds_clearance_business_days): struck with R3-A. No refund rule reads payoff channels any more.
- R3-B2 (state rate-filing day basis): cm_day_basis and cp_day_basis are removed. Every refund divides by the charge's actual period days, as the in-force "earned daily by actual days" rule requires.
- R3-B3 (7/10-day minimum policy terms): feed_min_term and fax_min_term are removed. The re-seeded feed and fax proofs are now month-to-month policies of more than binder_max_days.
- R3-C1 (day basis vs the base earning rule and "refunded in whole or in part"): closed with R3-B2. A refund can never exceed its charge, and an all-unearned period refunds exactly the charge.
- R3-C2 (rejected uploaded declarations page on a closed record falls under no rule): the upload rule's pick is the most recent upload. When that upload shows a period longer than binder_max_days, the outcome is not_applicable, and the compute enforces this. All three re-review tails now state that such uploads, like first reviews and agent-call proofs, are reviewed only on a tracking record that is not closed.
- R3-D1 (upload compute ignores the binder-only scope): the compute returns not_applicable when the latest upload is longer than binder_max_days. The unreachable binder-term step is removed from the order sentence. Probed with a later six-month declarations page and with a 38-day upload.
- R3-D2 (unstated "effective on or before the closed date"): the rule now defines two terms. A proof "counts" when it expires on or after the period start. A counting proof "reaches" the covered stretch when it also took effect on or before the closed_date. The compute uses exactly these two tests: the refund basis reads counting proofs, and the spans and gaps read reaching proofs.
- R3-D3 (tier-3/4 reads take every channel): every refund read now comes from the named insurer channel or from declarations_page_upload. The rule says "no proof of any other channel" and calls the upload channel "binder or declarations page alike", which matches the compute. The reinstatement tier is removed from the coverage ladder: a no-gap reinstatement always takes effect by the placement date, so the refund-basis method's full_no_lapse tier now carries it. Probed with extra accepted agent-call and other-insurer-channel proofs, neither of which is read.
- Class (scope vs compute on every channel read; every tier reachable and distinct): every ladder tier of all five rules was probed on scratch copies of both worlds. Each tier gives a value distinct from its fall-through, and each fall-through is reachable inside the rule's scope (plan.md "Round 5 probe table").
- Refund draw (4 each, at least 2 parameter and at least 1 method), all from the coordinator's list of real forms:
  - coverage counting (method; accepted earlier);
  - replacement grace keyed on the CPI plan;
  - renewal grace keyed on the contract state;
  - the charter's own refund bases (full_no_lapse / pro_rata_from_proof_effective / pro_rata_from_closure) as a method keyed on the counting proofs' effective dates against placement_effective_date and the closed date.
  - Credit tier no longer keys any refund ladder.
  - The refund tools now take refund_basis as an argument, so the basis written on the record follows the method.
- Re-review draw: feed and fax keep 6 factors each: model-year, loan-to-value and book-value allowances, credit-tier allowance, state expiry buffer, and reach date (method). The upload rule keeps 4. The tail sentence no longer claims the siblings apply "the same deductible allowances".
- Revision 1 and 2 classes are kept closed: no shares, credits, tenure grading, insurer-identity caps or interest. Contracts are unchanged and inside their tier limits. Personas were re-read: they state only the payoff and their own coverage start dates.
